claim: Jeff returns a probability for each listed option from a single forward pass, with no generated text.
quote: You describe a situation and list the options in plain words; Jeff returns a calibrated probability for each option from a single forward pass. No generated text, no parsing

claim: Author-reported speed is about 22 ms per decision on an RTX PRO 6000 and 28 ms on an Apple M4 Max.
quote:
about **22 ms** per
decision on an RTX PRO 6000 and **28 ms** on an Apple M4 Max (MLX)

claim: Speed was measured as the median over 200 benchmark questions of about 200 input tokens, one at a time.
quote:
Median time per decision over the same 200 benchmark questions (about 200 input tokens each), one question at a time,
from raw text to probabilities

claim: On CPU (32 threads) the 0.8B model takes 463 ms per decision.
The Jev latency comparison was not measured on the same hardware.
quote:
The
two times were not measured on the same hardware.

claim: Jeff is not affiliated with or endorsed by TypeSafe; it only shares Jev's request format.
quote:
Jeff uses the same request format as Jev, but it is not affiliated with or endorsed by TypeSafe, the
makers of Jev.

claim: Jeff's training code starts from the open-source AutoJev recipe by Denis Yarats.
quote: Jeff began as a fork of [AutoJev](https://github.com/denis-pplx/autojev) by Denis Yarats (MIT licence)

claim: Jev is TypeSafe AI's flagship model and uses choice/score/noul question types at a /v1/systemone endpoint.
quote: Jev is TypeSafe’s flagship model and the first System One model.

claim: TypeSafe's API endpoint is POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone.
quote: POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone

claim: Code is MIT licensed and model weights are Apache 2.0; training data is not released.
quote: Code: MIT (including AutoJev's). Model weights: Apache 2.0.

claim: The LICENSE names Mathias Strasser as Jeff's copyright holder.
quote: Copyright (c) 2026 Mathias Strasser (Jeff)

claim: Training used one RTX PRO 6000 GPU and synthetic data from an open model, with no cloud GPUs.
quote: No cloud GPUs, and no closed-model output in the training data

claim: On the author's 5-benchmark panel the 0.8B scores 79.1 and the 2B 82.0, vs Jev's published 83.0, measured on a different sample.
quote: The published Jev and AutoJev figures were measured on a different sample of the same benchmarks.

claim: Jeff trails well behind on reasoning benchmarks such as BBH and JevBench.
quote:
on the
reasoning-heavy benchmarks (BBH, JudgeBench, JevBench) it stays well below them, as you would expect at this size.

claim: v1.1 calibration error (ECE) is 0.021 for the 0.8B and 0.026 for the 2B.
v1.1 raised the option limit from 26 to 254.
quote: accept up to 254 options per question (v1.0: 26).

claim: v1.0 never picked options past the 26th, a bug reported by a user and fixed in v1.1.
quote: v1.0 never picked an option past the 26th, because no training question had more than 19 options

claim: MASSIVE and CLINC150 results are no longer zero-shot after v1.1.
quote: MASSIVE and CLINC150 results are no longer zero-shot.

claim: An outside user reproduced the benchmark-panel scores on v1.1.
quote: On the panel I get 79.1 and 81.9, matching your README.

claim: That user measured BANKING77 (not in training) rising to 66.2% (0.8B) and 64.9% (2B) in v1.1.
quote: BANKING77, which isn't in your training data, went from 23.4% to 66.2% (0.8B) and from 16.2% to 64.9% (2B)

claim: An HN user reported Jeff scoring 70% vs Jev's 94% on their own use cases.
quote: I compared it to Jev in my current use cases and it's very inaccurate. 70% vs 94% . for classification, it's unacceptable.

claim: Another HN user found the 0.8B useless for job-ad classification; the 2B was better but still missed job type.
quote: I tried the 0.8B model, completely useless in classification.

claim: The authors caution that small models do not reason and Jeff is English and text only.
quote: **Small models don't reason.**

claim: A voice-navigation fine-tune took held-out accuracy from 31.7% to 95.8% in under half an hour.
quote:
our
voice-navigation fine-tune moved held-out accuracy from 31.7% to 95.8% in under half an hour on one GPU

claim: The Jeff HN post drew 570 points and 222 comments (as of 2026-09-30).
quote: Jeff – Jev-compatible 0.8B decision models, trained at home, ~30 ms 570 222

claim: The repo had 1,176 GitHub stars as of 2026-09-30.
quote: 'stargazers_count': 1176

claim: Von is an Apache-2.0, 395M ModernBERT-based open decision model compatible with the TypeSafe protocol.
quote: Calibrated Choice / Noul / Score inference from a 395M ModernBERT encoder, one forward pass, CPU-served.

claim: Laya claims 32.8 ms on a single GPU, 100+ languages and Apache 2.0 weights.
quote: our models run in 32.8 milliseconds on a single GPU (7.2 ms/question batched)

claim: AutoJev-27B is a Qwen3.8-27B decision model with a TypeSafe-compatible API needing about 49 GiB of weights.
quote: a GPU with space for approximately 49 GiB of BF16 weights plus runtime overhead
